Early Solar System. A violent, chaotic period roughly four point six to four point five billion years ago when planets were still forming through collisions of planetary bodies. Massive impacts, including the giant impact that created Earth's moon, shaped planetary chemistry, structure, and the distribution of water and organic molecules across the terrestrial planets.

The solar system formed from a collapsing cloud of gas and dust roughly four point six billion years ago. Gravity concentrated material into the central sun and a swirling protoplanetary disk. Planetary embryos, sometimes called planetary seeds, grew to Mars-size within millions of years, then collided to form terrestrial planets like Earth.

These collisions were not gentle accumulations but violent impacts at orbital speeds. The impacts melted material and released enormous energy. The giant impact hypothesis proposes that a Mars-sized object called Theia struck Earth, ejecting debris that coalesced into the Moon.

Following the formation of the planets came the Late Heavy Bombardment, roughly four point one to three point eight billion years ago. This involved intense asteroid and comet impacts, possibly triggered by gravitational scattering of gas giants. These impacts delivered significant water, iron, and carbon-based compounds to Earth. Without them, Earth's oceans and life chemistry would be radically different.

Evidence from meteorites, lunar samples, and planetary physics shows that planetary migration and dynamical chaos were central to the Solar System's architecture. The giant planets likely migrated significantly from their birth locations, reshaping the entire system.

The Moon's origin was formed by the most dramatic impact of the early Solar System. The giant impact hypothesis is the model explaining Earth-Moon system formation. Planetary formation is the process that unfolded in this chaotic era. Theia was the Mars-sized impactor that shaped Earth. Impact craters are evidence of bombardment preserved on planetary surfaces. And the Hadean Eon is the geological eon encompassing the early Solar System's most violent phase.
